lesson_title: Vocabulary: Trade Terms, Tariffs & Trade Barriers

sections.title: GIỚI THIỆU
sections.body: Bài học đầu tiên của Unit 1 trang bị cho sinh viên FTU bộ từ vựng nền tảng về thương mại quốc tế — lĩnh vực trọng tâm của môn Tiếng Anh chuyên ngành. Hiểu đúng các thuật ngữ như tariff, quota, embargo hay FTA giúp bạn đọc hiểu hợp đồng, báo cáo thương mại và tham gia thảo luận chuyên môn bằng tiếng Anh. Bài này tập trung vào nhóm từ vựng về rào cản thương mại và các khái niệm liên quan, kèm câu mẫu và đoạn hội thoại ngắn để ghi nhớ ngữ cảnh sử dụng.

sections.title: LÝ THUYẾT CỐT LÕI
sections.body:
Core trade terms:

• Export / Import — goods or services sold to / bought from another country.
• Balance of trade — difference between a country's export and import values.
• Tariff — a tax imposed on imported goods; raises their price domestically.
• Quota — a quantitative limit on the volume of imports allowed.
• Embargo — a complete ban on trade with a specific country (often political).
• Subsidy — government financial support to domestic producers, making them more competitive abroad.
• Dumping — selling goods abroad below production cost or domestic price to gain market share.
• Anti-dumping duty — extra tariff imposed to counteract dumping.
• Free Trade Agreement (FTA) — pact between nations to reduce or eliminate tariffs and quotas.
• Most Favoured Nation (MFN) — WTO principle: a concession given to one member must be extended to all members.
• Non-tariff barrier (NTB) — regulations, standards, or procedures that restrict trade without a direct tax (e.g., sanitary standards, licensing requirements).
• Incoterms — international rules defining buyer/seller responsibilities for delivery, risk, and cost (e.g., FOB, CIF, EXW).

Phrase bank for discussion:
"The government imposed a 15% tariff on imported steel to protect domestic manufacturers."
"Under the ASEAN FTA, member states gradually eliminated tariffs on most goods."
"Non-tariff barriers such as complex customs procedures can be as restrictive as high duties."

sections.title: VÍ DỤ
sections.body:
Mini-dialogue — Trade policy meeting:

Manager: Our Vietnamese textile exports face a 12% tariff in the EU market. Have we explored duty-free access under the EVFTA?
Analyst: Yes. Under the agreement, tariffs on most textile products will be phased out over seven years. However, we must meet rules of origin — at least 40% of the product value must originate in Vietnam.
Manager: What about the US market?
Analyst: They imposed anti-dumping duties on certain categories last year. We may need to adjust pricing or source materials differently.

Sample sentences for practice:
1. The trade deficit widened because imports of electronic components increased sharply.
2. Quotas on agricultural imports were replaced by tariff-rate quotas under the new agreement.
3. Export subsidies are prohibited under WTO rules for most manufactured goods.

Fill-in exercise (answers in parentheses):
A ___ is a tax on imports. (tariff)
Selling below cost abroad is called ___. (dumping)
An ___ bans all trade with a country. (embargo)

sections.title: TÓM TẮT
sections.body:
Tariffs are price-based barriers; quotas are quantity-based; embargoes ban trade entirely.
FTAs reduce barriers between signatory countries; MFN ensures equal treatment among WTO members.
Non-tariff barriers include standards, licensing, and customs procedures — know Incoterms for contract language.
Practice using trade terms in full sentences, not isolated word lists.

lesson_title: Business Email: Inquiry, Quotation & Order Placement

sections.title: GIỚI THIỆU
sections.body: Thư tín thương mại (business correspondence) là kỹ năng then chốt trong môn Tiếng Anh chuyên ngành FTU. Ba loại email phổ biến nhất trong chuỗi giao dịch quốc tế là: thư hỏi giá (inquiry), thư báo giá (quotation) và thư đặt hàng (order). Bài học này cung cấp cấu trúc chuẩn, cụm từ chuyên ngành và mẫu email hoàn chỉnh để bạn viết trôi chảy, lịch sự và chính xác về mặt thương mại.

sections.title: LÝ THUYẾT CỐT LÕI
sections.body:
Standard email structure:
1. Subject line — clear and specific
2. Salutation — Dear Mr./Ms. [Name] / Dear Sir or Madam
3. Opening — state purpose immediately
4. Body — details, questions, or terms
5. Closing — call to action, polite sign-off
6. Signature — name, title, company, contact

Phrase bank — Inquiry:
• We are interested in purchasing… / We would like to request a quotation for…
• Please inform us of your best price, delivery time, and payment terms.
• Could you send us your latest catalogue and price list?
• We require approximately [quantity] units per month.

Phrase bank — Quotation:
• Further to your inquiry dated…, we are pleased to quote as follows.
• Unit price: USD [X] CIF Ho Chi Minh City / FOB [port].
• Delivery: within [X] weeks after receipt of order.
• Payment: 30% deposit, balance against shipping documents.
• This quotation is valid for 30 days.

Phrase bank — Order:
• We are pleased to place an order for the following items.
• Please confirm receipt of this order and advise the expected shipment date.
• Kindly arrange shipment via [carrier] to [destination].

sections.title: VÍ DỤ
sections.body:
Sample — Inquiry email:

Subject: Inquiry for Organic Robusta Coffee — 20 MT/month

Dear Ms. Tran,

We are a coffee roaster based in Hamburg and are interested in sourcing organic Robusta coffee from Vietnam. We would appreciate it if you could provide a quotation for 20 metric tons per month, CIF Hamburg.

Please include unit price, minimum order quantity, packaging specifications, and payment terms. We would also like to know whether your products hold organic certification (EU standard).

We look forward to your reply.

Yours sincerely,
Klaus Weber | Procurement Manager

Sample — Order confirmation (excerpt):

Subject: Purchase Order #PO-2026-0412 — Instant Coffee

Dear Mr. Nguyen,

Further to your quotation dated 15 March 2026, we confirm our order for 5,000 cartons of 3-in-1 instant coffee at USD 8.50/carton CIF Rotterdam. Shipment requested by 30 June 2026. Payment: irrevocable L/C at sight.

Please acknowledge receipt and send proforma invoice.

sections.title: TÓM TẮT
sections.body:
Inquiry emails ask for price, terms, and specifications — be specific about quantity and Incoterms.
Quotation emails respond with unit price, delivery, payment, and validity period.
Order emails confirm details from the quotation and request acknowledgment.
Keep tone formal, sentences concise; always include a clear subject line.

lesson_title: Techniques for Translating International Sales Contracts

sections.title: GIỚI THIỆU
sections.body: Unit 2 chuyển sang lĩnh vực ngân hàng, tài chính và chứng khoán, nhưng kỹ năng dịch thuật hợp đồng mua bán quốc tế là nền tảng chung cho mọi giao dịch thương mại. Sinh viên FTU cần nắm cấu trúc điều khoản hợp đồng tiếng Anh, nguyên tắc dịch thuật pháp lý và các thuật ngữ then chốt (force majeure, arbitration, governing law). Bài này đi sâu vào kỹ thuật dịch — không chỉ dịch từng từ mà chuyển đúng ý pháp lý và phong cách hợp đồng.

sections.title: LÝ THUYẾT CỐT LÕI
sections.body:
Principles of legal translation:

1. Accuracy over elegance — the legal effect must be preserved.
2. Consistency — translate the same term the same way throughout (e.g., always "Buyer" not alternating with "Purchaser" unless the source does).
3. Do not add or omit — if a clause is ambiguous in English, note it; do not resolve ambiguity in translation.
4. Use established Vietnamese legal terminology — refer to Luật Thương mại, Bộ luật Dân sự where applicable.

Key contract sections and translation notes:

• Preamble / Parties — "hereinafter referred to as" → "sau đây gọi là"
• Recitals (WHEREAS clauses) — background facts; translate in formal style
• Definitions — capitalised terms; create a glossary
• Subject matter & Specifications — precise product description
• Price & Payment — include currency, Incoterms, payment method (L/C, T/T)
• Delivery & Risk transfer — link to Incoterms 2020
• Warranties & Liability — limit of liability, indemnification
• Force majeure — events beyond control; standard lists (war, natural disaster, pandemic)
• Governing law & Dispute resolution — "governed by the laws of…" / "disputes shall be settled by arbitration under ICC rules"
• Termination — conditions for ending the contract

Common pitfalls:
— "Shall" = legal obligation (not merely "will").
— "Best endeavours" vs "reasonable endeavours" — different duty levels.
— "Without prejudice" — communications do not waive legal rights.

sections.title: VÍ DỤ
sections.body:
Source clause (English):
"The Seller shall deliver the Goods to the Buyer CIF Hai Phong port, Vietnam, in accordance with Incoterms 2020. Risk in the Goods shall pass to the Buyer when the Goods are loaded on board the vessel at the port of shipment."

Suggested translation (Vietnamese):
"Bên Bán phải giao Hàng hóa cho Bên Mua theo điều kiện CIF cảng Hải Phòng, Việt Nam, phù hợp Incoterms 2020. Rủi ro đối với Hàng hóa chuyển sang Bên Mua khi Hàng hóa được xếp lên tàu tại cảng xuất khẩu."

Practice — translate and identify key terms:
"In the event of force majeure, neither party shall be liable for failure to perform its obligations under this Agreement, provided that the affected party notifies the other party within fourteen (14) days."

(Answer sketch: force majeure = bất khả kháng; liable = chịu trách nhiệm; obligations = nghĩa vụ; notify = thông báo)

Glossary exercise — match:
Indemnify → bồi thường / bảo đảm bồi thường
Breach → vi phạm
Remedy → biện pháp khắc phục
Jurisdiction → thẩm quyền tài phán

sections.title: TÓM TẮT
sections.body:
Legal translation demands accuracy, consistency, and standard legal terminology — never creative paraphrase.
Know contract structure: parties, definitions, price, delivery, warranties, force majeure, governing law.
"Shall" expresses obligation; Incoterms define delivery and risk transfer precisely.
Build a glossary for each contract and maintain term consistency throughout.

sections.title: GIỚI THIỆU
sections.body: Unit 3 tập trung vào soạn thảo và dịch hợp đồng thương mại — kỹ năng nâng cao hơn Unit 2. Bài lý thuyết này trình bày khung cấu trúc hợp đồng quốc tế, nguyên tắc diễn đạt pháp lý tiếng Anh và sự khác biệt giữa các loại hợp đồng (sale of goods, distribution, agency). Đây là nền tảng trước khi sang bài tập vận dụng ở Lesson 2.

sections.title: LÝ THUYẾT CỐT LÕI
sections.body:
Types of international commercial contracts:

1. Sales Contract — one party sells goods to another; governed often by CISG (UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods) unless excluded.
2. Distribution Agreement — supplier appoints distributor in a territory; exclusive or non-exclusive.
3. Agency Agreement — agent acts on behalf of principal to procure sales; commission-based.
4. Licensing Agreement — grants IP rights (trademarks, patents) for use in a market.

Drafting principles:

• Clarity — one obligation per clause; avoid long compound sentences.
• Defined terms — capitalise and define in a Definitions section on first use.
• Active voice where possible — "The Seller shall deliver" not "Delivery shall be made by the Seller."
• Numbering — use hierarchical numbering (1, 1.1, 1.1.1) for cross-reference.
• Conditions precedent — events that must occur before obligation arises (e.g., L/C opened).

Essential clauses checklist:
□ Parties and capacity
□ Subject matter and quantity
□ Price, currency, and taxes
□ Payment terms and security (L/C, bank guarantee)
□ Delivery, Incoterms, and inspection
□ Title and risk transfer
□ Warranties (conformity, fitness for purpose)
□ Intellectual property (if applicable)
□ Confidentiality
□ Force majeure
□ Term and termination
□ Governing law and dispute resolution
□ Notices (addresses, method)
□ Entire agreement and amendments

Modal verbs in contracts:
— "shall" = mandatory duty
— "may" = permission / option
— "must not" / "shall not" = prohibition

sections.title: VÍ DỤ
sections.body:
Model clause — Definitions:
"'Agreement' means this International Sales Contract. 'Goods' means the products described in Schedule A. 'Business Day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday in Vietnam."

Model clause — Payment:
"The Buyer shall open an irrevocable Letter of Credit at sight in favour of the Seller for 100% of the Contract Price, payable against presentation of the documents listed in Clause 8. The L/C shall be established no later than fifteen (15) Business Days after the date of this Agreement."

Compare — weak vs strong drafting:
Weak: "The parties agree that delivery might happen around the end of the month."
Strong: "The Seller shall deliver the Goods on or before 30 April 2026. Time is of the essence."

Analysis question: Why is "Time is of the essence" important?
(Answer: It means late delivery is a material breach allowing the Buyer to terminate and claim damages, not merely a minor delay.)

sections.title: TÓM TẮT
sections.body:
Know contract types: sales, distribution, agency, licensing — each has distinct obligations.
Draft with defined terms, numbered clauses, and modal verbs used precisely (shall/may/shall not).
Essential clauses cover price, payment, delivery, warranties, force majeure, and dispute resolution.
"Time is of the essence" makes deadlines legally binding — use when punctuality is critical.

sections.title: GIỚI THIỆU
sections.body: Bài thực hành của Unit 3 yêu cầu bạn áp dụng kiến thức soạn thảo hợp đồng vào tình huống cụ thể: hoàn thiện điều khoản còn thiếu, sửa lỗi diễn đạt pháp lý và dịch đoạn hợp đồng sang tiếng Việt. Đây là dạng bài tập điển hình trong đề thi Tiếng Anh chuyên ngành FTU — tập trung vào kỹ năng vận dụng hơn là liệt kê lý thuyết.

sections.title: LÝ THUYẾT CỐT LÕI
sections.body:
Exercise 1 — Complete the clause:

"If the Buyer fails to open the Letter of Credit within the time specified in Clause 5, the Seller ___ the right to (a) extend the deadline by written notice, or (b) ___ this Agreement immediately without ___ to the Buyer."

(Answers: shall have / terminate / liability)

Exercise 2 — Identify errors in draft clause:

"The Seller maybe will try to deliver goods as soon as they can. Buyer can't complain if there is delay because of shipping problems."

Errors: informal tone ("maybe will try", "can't"); no fixed deadline; no force majeure procedure; unilateral exclusion of liability is likely unenforceable.

Rewritten:
"The Seller shall use reasonable endeavours to deliver the Goods by [date]. Neither party shall be liable for delay caused by force majeure events notified in accordance with Clause 12."

Exercise 3 — Translation (English → Vietnamese):

"This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, and agreements, whether written or oral."

Suggested: "Hợp đồng này cấu thành toàn bộ thỏa thuận giữa các Bên và thay thế mọi thương lượng, tuyên bố và thỏa thuận trước đây, dù bằng văn bản hay bằng lời."

sections.title: VÍ DỤ
sections.body:
Case study — Incomplete distribution agreement:

A Vietnamese company (Principal) drafts an agreement appointing a German distributor. The draft includes product list and territory (Germany, Austria) but omits:
— Minimum purchase targets
— Exclusivity terms
— Termination notice period
— Governing law

Task: Draft four clauses to fill these gaps.

Sample answers:

Exclusivity: "The Principal grants the Distributor the exclusive right to promote and sell the Products in the Territory during the Term, provided the Distributor achieves the Minimum Purchase Target in Schedule B."

Termination: "Either party may terminate this Agreement by giving ninety (90) days' prior written notice. Either party may terminate immediately upon material breach not remedied within thirty (30) days of written notice."

Governing law: "This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of Vietnam. Any dispute shall be referred to the Vietnam International Arbitration Centre (VIAC)."

sections.title: TÓM TẮT
sections.body:
Practice exercises: clause completion, error correction, translation, and gap-filling in real contract scenarios.
Avoid informal language and vague obligations — use "shall", fixed dates, and defined remedies.
Distribution agreements need exclusivity, targets, termination, and governing law clauses.
Always check: Who must do what, by when, and what happens if they don't?

sections.title: GIỚI THIỆU
sections.body: Unit 4 trang bị kỹ năng thuyết trình và đàm phán thương mại bằng tiếng Anh — năng lực then chốt khi sinh viên FTU thực tập tại doanh nghiệp xuất nhập khẩu hoặc tham gia hội chợ thương mại. Bài lý thuyết trình bày cấu trúc bài thuyết trình kinh doanh, ngôn ngữ persuasive và chiến lược đàm phán cơ bản (BATNA, anchoring, win-win). Nội dung chủ yếu bằng tiếng Anh để luyện tư duy trực tiếp trong môi trường quốc tế.

sections.title: LÝ THUYẾT CỐT LÕI
sections.body:
Presentation structure (10-minute pitch):

1. Hook / Opening — question, statistic, or story (30 sec)
2. Problem — pain point your audience faces (1 min)
3. Solution — your product/service (2 min)
4. Market & Evidence — size, growth, case studies (2 min)
5. Business model — how you make money (1 min)
6. Competitive advantage — why you, not rivals (1 min)
7. Call to action — what you want from the audience (1 min)
8. Q&A preparation

Language for presentations:
• "I'd like to draw your attention to…"
• "As you can see from this chart…"
• "This represents a 25% year-on-year increase."
• "To summarise the key takeaway…"
• "I'm happy to take questions."

Negotiation concepts:

• BATNA — Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement; your fallback if talks fail. Never accept a deal worse than your BATNA.
• ZOPA — Zone of Possible Agreement; overlap between both parties' acceptable ranges.
• Anchoring — first offer sets reference point; research supports making a reasonable but ambitious opening.
• Win-win — expand the pie (long-term partnership, volume discounts) rather than zero-sum haggling.
• Active listening — "If I understand correctly, your main concern is delivery time, not price."

Cultural awareness: In many Asian contexts, relationship-building precedes hard bargaining; allow time for trust. In direct cultures, clarity and speed are valued.

sections.title: VÍ DỤ
sections.body:
Opening script — Export pitch for Vietnamese cashews:

"Good morning. Vietnam is the world's largest cashew exporter, yet less than 15% reaches the premium organic segment in Europe. Today I'll show how our cooperative in Binh Phuoc delivers certified organic cashews with full traceability — and why three EU retailers have already placed trial orders."

Negotiation dialogue:

Buyer: Your price is 10% above the market average.
Seller: I understand price sensitivity. Our product includes organic certification and vacuum packaging, which reduces spoilage by 40%. Could we explore a two-year contract with quarterly volumes of 50 MT? We can offer a 6% discount at that volume.
Buyer: We were thinking 35 MT per quarter.
Seller: At 40 MT we can match 7% discount and extend payment to 60 days. Would that work?

Phrase for handling objections:
"I appreciate your concern. Let me address that by showing…"
"What would need to be true for this proposal to work for you?"

sections.title: TÓM TẮT
sections.body:
Structure presentations: hook → problem → solution → evidence → CTA.
Know BATNA (your walk-away point) and ZOPA (overlap zone) before negotiating.
Use anchoring strategically; seek win-win through volume, payment terms, or long-term deals.
Active listening and cultural awareness strengthen international negotiations.

sections.title: GIỚI THIỆU
sections.body: Bài thực hành Unit 4 đưa bạn vào hai tình huống: soạn outline thuyết trình 5 phút cho sản phẩm xuất khẩu Việt Nam và role-play đàm phán giá-lô hàng. Đây là dạng bài tập mang tính kỹ năng cao — yêu cầu viết và nói bằng tiếng Anh tự nhiên, có cấu trúc và chiến lược rõ ràng.

sections.title: LÝ THUYẾT CỐT LÕI
sections.body:
Task A — Write a 5-slide outline for presenting Vietnamese dragon fruit to a Japanese supermarket buyer.

Slide 1: Title — "Premium Red-Flesh Dragon Fruit from Long An Province"
Slide 2: Market trend — Japan's demand for exotic fruit grew 8% annually; red variety is rare.
Slide 3: Product — GAP-certified, air-freight ready, shelf life 14 days with cold chain.
Slide 4: Pricing — USD 4.20/kg FOB Tan Son Nhat; trial order 2 MT; 5% discount at 10 MT/month.
Slide 5: Next steps — sample shipment, store trial in Tokyo, quarterly review.

Task B — Negotiation role-play cards:

Seller (Vietnamese rice exporter):
— Target price: USD 520/MT FOB
— Floor price: USD 495/MT
— BATNA: existing buyer at USD 490/MT
— Can offer: 2% discount for 500+ MT, 45-day payment

Buyer (Philippine distributor):
— Target price: USD 480/MT
— Ceiling: USD 510/MT
— BATNA: Thai supplier at USD 505/MT
— Needs: delivery within 30 days, quality certificate

Task C — Persuasive phrases (fill in):
1. Our quality control exceeds ___ standards. (Answer: international / ASEAN)
2. We're confident this partnership will ___ mutual growth. (drive / deliver)
3. Let's ___ a pilot shipment before committing to annual volume. (arrange / propose)

sections.title: VÍ DỤ
sections.body:
Sample negotiation transcript:

Buyer: We need 300 MT of 5% broken rice, delivery to Manila within 30 days. Our budget is USD 485 per ton.
Seller: For 300 MT we can offer USD 515 FOB Ho Chi Minh City, including quality inspection certificate. Delivery in 25 days.
Buyer: That's above our Thai quote of USD 505.
Seller: Our rice has lower moisture content — 12% vs industry 14% — giving you better yield. At 400 MT, we can do USD 508.
Buyer: We can commit to 350 MT if you meet USD 500.
Seller: Agreed at USD 500 for 350 MT, payment by L/C at sight, shipment by 20 May. I'll send the contract today.

Debrief questions:
1. What was the Seller's BATNA? (USD 490 existing buyer)
2. Did they stay above BATNA? (Yes — USD 500 > USD 490)
3. What win-win element appeared? (Volume commitment unlocked lower price)

sections.title: TÓM TẮT
sections.body:
Presentation practice: 5-slide outline with hook, product proof, pricing, and clear next steps.
Negotiation practice: know your BATNA, floor/ceiling, and tradeable variables (volume, payment, delivery).
Role-play builds fluency — use data (yield, certification) to justify price, not emotion.
Debrief every negotiation: Did we beat BATNA? What concessions were exchanged?

chapter_title: Bộ đề thi Tiếng Anh chuyên ngành FTU
lesson_title: Bài 1: Tài liệu ôn tập & đề thi

sections.title: GIỚI THIỆU
sections.body: Chương cuối tổng hợp dạng đề thi Tiếng Anh chuyên ngành FTU: trắc nghiệm từ vựng, điền từ, dịch đoạn văn, viết email/hợp đồng ngắn và đọc hiểu chuyên ngành. Bài này cung cấp đề mẫu với đáp án để bạn tự luyện trước kỳ thi — độ khó và phạm vi kiến thức bao trùm Unit 1–4.

sections.title: LÝ THUYẾT CỐT LÕI
sections.body:
PART A — Multiple choice (Vocabulary):

1. A tax on imported goods is called a:
   a) quota  b) tariff  c) subsidy  d) embargo
   Answer: b

2. "CIF" under Incoterms 2020 means the seller pays:
   a) only ex-factory cost  b) cost, insurance, and freight to destination port
   c) customs duty at destination  d) import VAT
   Answer: b

3. "Force majeure" refers to:
   a) intentional breach  b) events beyond reasonable control  c) price adjustment  d) quality inspection
   Answer: b

PART B — Fill in the blank:

The Buyer shall open an irrevocable Letter of ___ at sight. (Credit)
Under the FTA, ___ on most goods will be eliminated by 2028. (tariffs)
Neither party shall be ___ for delay caused by force majeure. (liable)

PART C — Reading comprehension (excerpt):
"The ASEAN Free Trade Area has significantly reduced tariffs among member states. However, non-tariff barriers remain, including differing product standards and customs documentation requirements."

Q: What problem does the passage mention besides tariffs?
A: Non-tariff barriers (standards, customs documentation).

sections.title: VÍ DỤ
sections.body:
PART D — Translation (Vietnamese → English):

Source: "Bên Bán cam kết giao hàng đúng chất lượng và số lượng theo hợp đồng. Trong trường hợp bất khả kháng, bên bị ảnh hưởng phải thông báo cho bên kia trong vòng 7 ngày."

Model answer: "The Seller undertakes to deliver goods in conformity with the quality and quantity specified in the Contract. In the event of force majeure, the affected party shall notify the other party within seven (7) days."

PART E — Email writing (15 marks):

Task: Write an inquiry email (80–100 words) to a Malaysian palm oil supplier. Include: product grade, quantity (50 MT/month), requested price CIF Hai Phong, and payment terms.

Sample opening: "Dear Sir or Madam, We are a food processing company in Vietnam seeking a reliable supplier of refined palm oil (CP8 grade), approximately 50 MT per month, CIF Hai Phong port…"

Scoring guide: format (3), vocabulary (4), grammar (4), completeness (4).

sections.title: TÓM TẮT
sections.body:
Exam covers: MCQ vocabulary, fill-in-blank, reading, translation (Vi↔En), and practical writing (email/clause).
